title: Minimizing Logistics API Exposure
business: A regional logistics provider managing a fleet of delivery drones and warehouse robots.
problem: The company exposes a monolithic API that includes administrative endpoints, public tracking interfaces, and internal sensor telemetry, creating an unnecessarily large attack surface that invites lateral movement.
solution: By applying the Economy of Mechanism and Least Privilege principles, the company decomposes the monolith into micro-services, ensuring each interface only exposes the minimum functionality required for its specific role, effectively shrinking the reachable attack surface.
steps: Audit all existing API endpoints to categorize them by user role and functional necessity.
Implement an API Gateway to act as a single, hardened entry point that enforces strict routing.
Apply the principle of Least Privilege by restricting internal telemetry endpoints to local network segments only.
Remove unused legacy debugging interfaces and deprecated functions to reduce the total code complexity.
Establish a continuous monitoring process to verify that new code deployments do not introduce unauthorized reachable interfaces.
outcome: A significantly reduced number of exposed entry points, making it harder for attackers to discover and exploit sensitive internal administrative functions.
limitation: Aggressive compartmentalization can increase operational complexity, requiring robust service discovery and monitoring to ensure that legitimate inter-service communication is not inadvertently blocked.
